verdict.analysis:
Response A claims to have cleaned the files but the execution was incomplete and problematic. The run ended abnormally ('turn_cap did not finish normally'), backup files were left in the proofs/ directory despite the user's explicit instruction to overwrite in place with no duplicates, and the final cleanup command failed. File size changes (label_back.jpg +2225 bytes, moodboard.webp +2222 bytes) indicate re-encoding occurred, violating the colour-preservation requirement. While A claims ICC profiles are identical via MD5 hashes, the significant size increases contradict this claim. A provides minimal verification detail for rights metadata preservation.

Response B successfully completed the task with no abnormal termination. All backup files were removed, leaving only the cleaned production files in proofs/. File size changes are consistent with metadata removal only (label_back.jpg reduced to 21546 bytes, moodboard.webp to 1580 bytes). B explicitly verified AI signature removal via strings, exiftool, and hex inspection across all files. B added required rights/credit metadata to files that lacked it and verified preservation of existing rights in the sidecar. B provided detailed per-file verification in both the chat response and comprehensive documentation files (README_CLEAN.txt and VERIFICATION_REPORT.txt). The actions_taken log shows successful completion of all operations with proper verification steps.

The user's core requirement was: "i'd rather you tell me it's clean because you went and looked than because a tool said so." B demonstrates this through explicit manual verification steps (strings scans, hex inspection, trailer checks, exiftool full metadata dumps) and reports findings per file. A relies more on tool output without demonstrating the same level of manual inspection and leaves the job incomplete with backups still present.
